account:
Today seems fairly routine so far. I attended the morning market walk and have returned to town hall at one for accounts after going home for the noon lunch appointment. The baker reported stocking thirty-two fresh loaves at one emerald each and no town problem. Residents mentioned seeing the baker carrying wheat at the bakery and bread at the inn; I also saw bread being placed in the stall chest. This appears consistent with ordinary baking and deliveries, not evidence of anything improper. The baker asked whether upcoming gatherings would require extra loaves; I know of none and made no order.

The builder came seeking a paid repair commission, with locations, standards and an approved price. I requested a safety inspection and itemized estimate rather than authorizing paid construction. My later attempt to specify a bridge inspection and a one-o'clock report was not heard, so I cannot assume the builder knows those details. The secretary said there was no existing repair list or approved budget and told the builder to obtain my authorization.

The unresolved oddity is my three-o'clock tea appointment: the book says only a neighbour at a dockside cottage on the east bank, with no name or exact address. The secretary promised to investigate, but I have not received confirmation. I asked market residents and the baker without hearing a definite answer. I heard the baker speaking as I left but could not make out the words, so that may have contained information I missed. The secretary is now visible near the hall with a writable book. I should ask about accounts and the tea address, then attend tea and return for the four-thirty office appointment.
